annotations.title: Unified Ptolemy via curvatureSin: Module Overview and Proof Chain
annotations.content:
This synthesis file introduces curvatureSin K — the sn_K function from constant-curvature geometry — and shows how it unifies Ptolemy-type theorems across spherical (K>0), Euclidean (K=0), and hyperbolic (K<0) geometries. The module docstring (lines 7-65) describes six results: the K=0,1,-1 special cases, the zero-at-zero property, the spherical Ptolemy equality, and the new spherical Ptolemy INEQUALITY.

The proof chain for the key new result (spherical_ptolemy_ineq_curvatureSin) is spelled out in the docstring: (1) curvatureSin 1 t = sin t, (2) chord-arc identity converts sin values to half chord lengths, (3) the inequality becomes (||z1-z3||/2)(||z2-z4||/2) ≤ ..., (4) divide ptolemy_inequality by 4.

The distinction between EQUALITY (requires concyclicity, from PtolemysTheoremOQ01OQ02.lean) and INEQUALITY (unconditional, proved here) is the central conceptual contribution. Lines 59-65 explain why the K=-1 case remains a conjecture: the Poincaré disk metric requires ~800-1200 lines of infrastructure not yet in Mathlib.
annotations.mathContext: The sn_K function from constant-curvature geometry: $sn_K(t) = \sin(\sqrt{K}\cdot t)/\sqrt{K}$ for $K>0$, $sn_0(t) = t$ (Euclidean limit), $sn_K(t) = \sinh(\sqrt{|K|}\cdot t)/\sqrt{|K|}$ for $K<0$. The unified Ptolemy equality: $sn_K(d_{ac}/2)\cdot sn_K(d_{bd}/2) = sn_K(d_{ab}/2)\cdot sn_K(d_{cd}/2) + sn_K(d_{ad}/2)\cdot sn_K(d_{bc}/2)$ for cyclic quadrilaterals in $\kappa$-geometry. The chord-arc identity $\|z_i - z_j\| = 2\sin(\arccos(\langle z_i,z_j\rangle)/2)$ for unit-circle points is the key bridge between the metric and the algebraic form.

annotations.title: curvatureSin: Three-Way If-Then-Else Definition
annotations.content:
The curvatureSin K t definition (lines 87-90) uses a three-way if-then-else: if K = 0 then t; else if 0 < K then sin(√K · t) / √K; else sinh(√(-K) · t) / √(-K). The `noncomputable` annotation is required because Real.sin and Real.sqrt are noncomputable.

The K<0 branch writes √(-K) to avoid imaginary square roots. Since K<0 implies -K>0, √(-K) is a well-defined real number.

The K=0 case is the continuous limit: as K→0, sin(√K·t)/√K → t by L'Hôpital's rule. The Lean definition avoids division-by-zero by treating K=0 as a special case rather than a limit, which is why the `if K = 0` branch comes first.
annotations.mathContext: $sn_K(t) = \begin{cases} \sin(\sqrt{K}\cdot t)/\sqrt{K} & K > 0 \\ t & K = 0 \\ \sinh(\sqrt{|K|}\cdot t)/\sqrt{|K|} & K < 0 \end{cases}$. The K→0 limit: $\lim_{K\to 0} \frac{\sin(\sqrt{K}\cdot t)}{\sqrt{K}} = \lim_{u\to 0} \frac{\sin(u)}{u}\cdot t = t$ (L'Hôpital). This continuity makes K=0 the flat (Euclidean) limit of both spherical and hyperbolic geometry.

annotations.title: Special Case Lemmas: simp Proofs and Proof Patterns
annotations.content:
Five lemmas establish the special cases of curvatureSin. The proof patterns reveal Lean's branching tactics:

- curvatureSin_zero (line 99): `simp [curvatureSin]` — K=0 branch taken.
- curvatureSin_pos (line 104): `simp only [..., if_neg (ne_of_gt hK), if_pos hK]` — both branching conditions unfolded from hK : 0 < K.
- curvatureSin_neg (line 109): Similar using hK : K < 0 and `not_lt.mpr`.
- curvatureSin_one (line 115): `rw [curvatureSin_pos one_pos, Real.sqrt_one, one_mul, div_one]` — chains three steps: √1=1, 1·t=t, t/1=t.
- curvatureSin_neg_one (line 121): Adds `have h : -(-1:ℝ) = 1` then rewrites √1=1.
- curvatureSin_zero_right (line 128): `unfold curvatureSin; split_ifs <;> simp [Real.sin_zero, Real.sinh_zero]` — splits all branches simultaneously.

The `@[simp]` attribute on curvatureSin_zero and curvatureSin_zero_right makes them automatically applicable in downstream theorem proofs.
annotations.mathContext: $sn_1(t) = \sin(\sqrt{1}\cdot t)/\sqrt{1} = \sin(t)/1 = \sin(t)$. $sn_{-1}(t) = \sinh(\sqrt{1}\cdot t)/\sqrt{1} = \sinh(t)$. $sn_K(0) = 0$ for all $K$: all three cases give 0 at $t=0$ ($\sin(0)=0$, $0=0$, $\sinh(0)=0$). The value $sn_K(0)=0$ reflects that all three geometries have zero arc length from a point to itself.

annotations.title: Spherical Ptolemy Equality: One-Line Proof via curvatureSin_one
annotations.content:
The spherical Ptolemy equality theorem (lines 156-165) is stated for four unit-sphere points a,b,c,d in an abstract real inner product space V (declared via the variable block at line 136). This is more general than the complex case in the inequality theorem.

The proof is two lines: `simp only [curvatureSin_one]` reduces all curvatureSin 1 _ to sin _, leaving the goal exactly as `SphericalPtolemy.spherical_ptolemy`. Then `exact SphericalPtolemy.spherical_ptolemy h_cosph h_apc h_bpd ha hb hc hd` closes by delegation.

The theorem requires both Cospherical (the four points lie on a common circle) AND angle conditions h_apc, h_bpd (the diagonals AC and BD cross at p). These are the concyclicity hypotheses the inequality theorem drops.

The abstract inner product space V allows this theorem for any sphere in any finite-dimensional real inner product space, not just the unit circle in ℂ — generality the inequality theorem (which uses complex ptolemy_inequality) does not achieve.
annotations.mathContext: $sn_1(d(a,c)/2)\cdot sn_1(d(b,d)/2) = sn_1(d(a,b)/2)\cdot sn_1(d(c,d)/2) + sn_1(d(a,d)/2)\cdot sn_1(d(b,c)/2)$ where $d(x,y) = \arccos(\langle x,y\rangle)$. Concyclicity conditions: `Cospherical ({a,b,c,d} : Set V)` = the four points lie on a common circle; $\angle apC = \pi$ and $\angle bpd = \pi$ = p is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD.

annotations.title: Spherical Ptolemy Inequality: Chord-Arc Bridge to Complex Ptolemy
annotations.content:
The key new result: the spherical Ptolemy inequality for all four unit-circle points in ℂ, no concyclicity needed. The proof (lines 197-229) has a five-step structure:

1. `simp only [curvatureSin_one]` reduces sin values, goal becomes a sin inequality.
2. Six `have` statements (lines 200-211) apply `SphericalPtolemy.unit_sphere_chord_via_sin` to each of the six pairs, yielding ||z_i - z_j|| = 2·sin(...).
3. Six more `have` statements (lines 213-218) rearrange to sin(...) = ||z_i - z_j|| / 2 via `linarith`.
4. `rw [s13, s24, s12, s34, s23, s14]` substitutes all sin values with half-norms.
5. `have hP := ptolemy_inequality z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄` (line 223) imports the complex inequality; ring+linarith closes via division by 4.

The `ring` lemmas at lines 225-227 are the algebraic bridge: (a/2)·(b/2) = ab/4, so after substitution the goal is exactly hP/4.
annotations.mathContext: For $z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4 \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\|z_i\|=1$: $\sin(d_{13}/2)\cdot\sin(d_{24}/2) \leq \sin(d_{12}/2)\cdot\sin(d_{34}/2) + \sin(d_{23}/2)\cdot\sin(d_{14}/2)$. Chord-arc: $\|z-w\| = 2\sin(\arccos(\mathrm{Re}(\bar{z}w))/2)$ for unit-circle points. After substituting $\sin(d_{ij}/2) = \|z_i-z_j\|/2$, the inequality becomes $\|z_1-z_3\|\cdot\|z_2-z_4\| \leq \|z_1-z_2\|\cdot\|z_3-z_4\| + \|z_2-z_3\|\cdot\|z_1-z_4\|$ (dividing ptolemy_inequality by 4).

annotations.title: Hyperbolic Case: Infrastructure Gap and Mathlib Roadmap
annotations.content:
Lines 231-257 analyze why the K=-1 (hyperbolic) Ptolemy theorem is currently unavailable. The conjecture: for four points on a common hyperbolic circle in the Poincaré disk D={z : ℂ | ||z|| < 1}, sinh(d_H(z1,z3)/2)·sinh(d_H(z2,z4)/2) equals the sum formula using curvatureSin (-1) = sinh.

The blocking identity is the hyperbolic chord-arc: sinh(d_H(z,w)/2) = |z-w|/√((1-|z|²)(1-|w|²)). This requires: (1) Poincaré disk metric as a metric space (~300 lines), (2) Möbius transformations as hyperbolic isometries (~400-500 lines), (3) hyperbolic circle = Euclidean circle plus conformal factor cancellation (~200 lines). Total: ~800-1200 lines not in Mathlib.

The structural difference from the spherical case: in the spherical chord-arc ||z-w|| = 2·sin(d(z,w)/2) for unit-circle points, the 'conformal factor' is 1 and cancels trivially. In the hyperbolic case, the factor (1-|z|²)^(1/2) depends on z and only cancels for points on a common hyperbolic circle.

Lines 259-270 give seven #check statements verifying all definitions and theorems have the expected polymorphic types.
annotations.mathContext: Hyperbolic chord-arc in the Poincaré disk: $\sinh(d_H(z,w)/2) = \frac{|z-w|}{\sqrt{(1-|z|^2)(1-|w|^2)}}$ where $d_H(z,w) = 2\tanh^{-1}\!\left(\frac{|z-w|}{|1-\bar{z}w|}\right)$. For points on a hyperbolic circle centered at 0: $|z_i| = \tanh(r/2)$ is constant, so $(1-|z_i|^2) = \mathrm{sech}^2(r/2)$ cancels in the product formula. This conformal factor cancellation is the content of the blocked infrastructure step.
